newsitem.title: USA: New Democratic Party head vows clean fundraising.
newsitem.headline: New Democratic Party head vows clean fundraising.

text.p: Colorado Gov. Roy Romer, tapped by President Clinton as the new chairman of the Democratic National Committee, vowed Wednesday an end to improper campaign fundraising, an issue that has plagued his party.

"The Democratic Party made some mistakes, serious errors that need to be corrected," Romer told reporters in his office at the capitol. He said new rules on campaign finance were being drawn up and will be announced in "five to seven days."

Romer, in his third term as governor, also said he has not ruled out running for the Senate in 1998 for the seat held by Ben Nighthorse Campbell, a former Democrat who switched to the Republican Party. But he said it would be difficult to run for office while running the state and the Democratic Party.
Romer also said Clinton originally asked him to resign as governor to dedicate his full time to the party job. "I felt I couldn't give up the governorship," he said.
Steve Grossman, a Massachusetts businessman and Democratic Party activist, will head up day-to-day operations at the DNC.

Romer conceded that despite the need to make changes in how the party raises funds, one of his main tasks will be to canvass the country raising money. He said he believed the party was about $10 million in debt and said he would "play cleanly and legally" in helping to raise money.

He had been rumoured for a spot in the Cabinet in Clinton's second term, at least in local political circles. But Colorado went for Republican candidate Bob Dole in the Nov. 5 election and the Democratic candidate for an open U.S. Senate seat in Colorado lost to Republican Representative Wayne Allard.
